title: `Worker` inside `SharedWorker`
body:
### What is the issue with the HTML Standard?

Currently `Worker` can only be spawned from a global scope (tab) and cannot be spawned from a `SharedWorker`.

### Use Case

Take this example - a finance tracking application that uses the storage model of the pre-saas era. Namely, user data is physically on the user's device and the application does not offer cloud storage (you can technically save it to a network drive or Google Drive on your disk, but that's an OS concern).

Uses would:
- Open a file (persistent handle)
- Make changes
- Changes auto save to disk as you make changes (not periodic sync)

### What does that have to do with nesting `Worker` within `SharedWorker`? 

Say I want to use a storage format like SQLite or some other similar database engine (via wasm). You can use the origin private file system API, specifically `fileHandle.createSyncAccessHandle()` to gain access to a file handle. This, however, is only available in a DedicatedWorker.  

In a finance management application, users will often want to open multiple tabs to cross reference between accounts, view reports, searches, update categories etc.

A `SharedWorker` allows all tabs to serialize queries to a single data management service (creating effectively an in-browser database engine). 

However, `SharedWorker` does not have access to the `createSyncAccessHandle` because it's a blocking call. This necessitates using a `Worker` as the owner of that file handle, passing it to the `SharedWorker`. `SharedWorker` cannot create a DedicatedWorker so this pattern is either impossible or unmaintainable (coordinating the filehandle access between dedicated workers on tabs and routing requests to the correct worker).

This could be mitigated by simply spawning a `Worker` within a `SharedWorker`. Or perhaps creating a `fileHandle.createAsyncAccessHandle()` that can be accessed within a `SharedWorker`
